content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Software stripe

Let's take a closer look at what each of these platforms offers. Stripe is a payment gateway that allows businesses to accept online payments. PayPal is a digital wallet that enables individuals and businesses to send and receive payments. Gumroad is a platform that makes it easy for creators to sell digital products. Lemon Squeezy is an e-commerce platform that allows businesses to create and manage their online stores. And Paddle is a platform that helps developers sell their software and handle customer support. Each of these platforms has its own set of features, fees, and requirements, but they all share one common trait: they're not available in every country, and they often come with restrictions and limitations.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

So, how do these platforms handle restricted countries? Stripe operates in 46 countries out of 195 on earth, which means that if you're in one of the 149 countries where Stripe is not available, you're out of luck. PayPal, on the other hand, has a history of suspending accounts without warning, and in some countries, they even hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle also have their own set of restrictions and limitations, and they might not be available in your country either. In some cases, you might be able to use alternative payment methods, but these often come with high fees and limited functionality.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Another important aspect to consider is payment speed, fees, and real costs. Stripe charges a flat rate of 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction, while PayPal charges 2.9% + 30¢ for domestic transactions and 4.4% + 30¢ for international transactions. Gumroad charges a flat rate of 3.5% + 30¢ per transaction, while Lemon Squeezy charges a flat rate of 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction. Paddle charges a flat rate of 5% + 30¢ per transaction. In addition to these fees, you also need to consider the costs of payment processing, transaction fees, and any other fees associated with using these platforms.
Stripe's geographic exclusion list is a deliberate infrastructure decision — not a temporary gap waiting to be fixed.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When it comes to ownership, automation, and delivery, things get even more complicated. With Stripe, you have to set up your own payment gateway, which means handling transactions, managing refunds, and dealing with customer support. With PayPal, you have to deal with account suspensions, reversals, and limited functionality. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle might offer more automation and delivery options, but they often come with their own set of limitations and restrictions.

If you're in a country where Stripe or PayPal is not available, you might want to consider an alternative like Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which offers a fully customizable e-commerce platform that integrates with multiple payment gateways, including NOWPayments. With Edge Commerce Stack, you get a 100% customizable store, automated delivery, and real-time analytics, all without relying on Stripe or any other platform. In the end, the choice depends on your specific needs and requirements, but it's essential to carefully evaluate the pros and cons of each option before making a decision.

This way, you can sell software and handle customer support without relying on Stripe or any other platform.
